entries.title: Agamemnon
entries.text:
Agamemnon

Agamemnon, the agamemnon look, is a named grade of hard sun, bronze bounce, and a dusk sky the color of a bruise, so a living body reads as antique metal. The name is not a shot: you still lock a height, pick a lens, and place a figure who can hold that weather.

Create this Agamemnon

Narrative function

Use it on a beat where the person is already doomed and the sky agrees. A rider on a ridge, a man on an empty platform, a coat at a parapet: the camera stays mostly still so metal and dusk can do the sentence.

Scale may go statue-large or map-small. Either is legal if the sun is hard and the fill never turns the face into a beauty still.

It is the wrong tool when the scene needs charm, flirtation, or a clean key. Pour it on a rom-com and you get a perfume ad with extra dirt, or a tragedy nobody asked for.

How it works

Lock off, or use a slow push that does not steal the grade. Eye height to slightly low, 35mm to 50mm so faces do not melt.

Key is hard sun or a hard HMI from camera-left or behind. Bounce is warm dust, bronze, or iron, not a white card.

Shadows stay opaque. No neon, no beauty dish.

Then prompt: Agamemnon look on [Subject], bronze, blood-dusk, tragic scale, a king under a bad sky, antique epic as grade. Name the stand, the key side, and what must stay readable.

When to use it

A myth, a war portrait, or a contemporary face that should feel cursed: the rider pauses on the ridge and the citadel below already looks like a tomb. Do not use it as a default warm LUT on any wide.

Compared with similar shots

Spaghetti Western shares hard sun and dust, but its moral weather is frontier irony, not antique bronze. Hard Light is the lamp without the metal-and-dusk law.

Knight's Diary is the same period hunger written as gold leaf and mud on a page, not as a king under a bad sky.

Spaghetti WesternMyth in dirt.

Hard LightGrit, noon sun, or interrogation.

Ink RiotThe image should spill.

In film

Troy gives the sun-and-metal grammar. The Northman gives mud, iron, and a face that already lost.

Borrow light and metal, not a copyrighted still.

Prompt it

Lead with the person and the stand, then the grade. Example: Agamemnon look on [Subject], bronze, blood-dusk, tragic scale, a king under a bad sky, antique epic as grade.

Add hard sun camera-left, opaque shadows, 35mm, eye height, no neon. Do not write mood words in place of the key.

Use in Image Generator

Agamemnon look on [Subject], bronze, blood-dusk, tragic scale, a king under a bad sky, antique epic as grade.

What usually goes wrong

The usual cousin is a generic teal-and-gold prestige still, or a Hard Light beauty portrait. The tell is perfume-ad skin and a sky that is only pretty.

Fix it: name bronze, bruise dusk, and a figure small or statue-large, then kill the fill.

Questions

What is Agamemnon in film?

A named grade, not a camera move: hard sun, bronze bounce, and a bruise-colored dusk that makes a living body read as antique metal. You still have to choose height, lens, and subject.

Agamemnon vs Hard Light

Hard light is any small, sharp source. Agamemnon is that hardness plus bronze skin-lights and a dusk that already judges the person. If you only spec a hard key, you have not asked for this look.

When should I use Agamemnon?

On a tragic or mythic beat where the sky should feel wrong: a king, a rider, a modern portrait that wants to feel cursed. Skip it for flirtation, comedy, and clean fashion keys.

How do I prompt Agamemnon for AI image or video?

Write the subject, camera height, and hard sun first, then the grade clause: Agamemnon look on [Subject], bronze, blood-dusk, tragic scale, a king under a bad sky, antique epic as grade. Lock the camera. No neon.

entries.title: Ink Riot
entries.text:
Ink Riot

Ink riot, the ink riot effect, is liquid calligraphy occupying the air around a still-photographic subject: black and color blooming, dripping, exploding off a brush. The camera still needs a stand and a readable face, because the ink is weather, not a texture pack.

Volume

Create this Ink Riot

Narrative function

The shot is a page that fought back. Hold the person.

Let ink do the violence: a bloom past the cheek, a splash that hides a doorway, a black tide that has not yet reached the eyes. Titles, music, and a character whose interior is a mess can survive this.

Procedural crime coverage usually cannot, unless you are in the credits. It is the wrong tool when you need geography, eyelines, or a clean insert.

If the face drowns, you shot a stock loop of paint, not a scene.

How it works

Lock off, or use a tiny handheld that does not chase every splash. Eye height, 35mm to 50mm, subject sharp.

Key is a real lamp (sodium, window, practical) so the photographic body has a shadow. Describe ink as matter: blooming, dripping, occupying air.

One palette, not every hue. Keep eyes clear.

Prompt: Ink riot around [Subject], black and color blooming in liquid, calligraphy as explosion, a page that fights.

When to use it

A title card, a breakdown, a music still where the room should spill. Do not use it on a two-shot that has to cut on dialogue.

Compared with similar shots

Collage is cut paper and edges, dry pieces, not liquid. Mixed Media stacks stocks and techniques.

Akrill is thick paint sitting on the world. Ink riot is airborne calligraphy around a face that still photographs.

CollageOne image is not enough; stack them.

Mixed MediaNo single medium owns the truth.

AgamemnonMake them ancient and doomed.

In film

Zhang Yimou's Hero uses ink-in-water as weather around bodies. Sin City titles treat ink as the world.

The still should look wet. You are borrowing the liquid law, not a frame.

Prompt it

Hold a readable subject, then the liquid. Ink riot around [Subject], black and color blooming in liquid, calligraphy as explosion, a page that fights.

Add lock-off, key side, and which features must stay dry. For motion, ink blooms and settles.

The person does not dissolve.

Use in Image Generator

Ink riot around [Subject], black and color blooming in liquid, calligraphy as explosion, a page that fights.

What usually goes wrong

Models drown the subject or add Comic halftone and oil at once. The tell is no eyes, or every medium in one frame.

Fix it: one ink palette, photographic face, lock-off, ink as matter in air.

Questions

What is Ink Riot in film?

A graphic look where ink behaves as weather around a photographic subject: blooming, dripping calligraphy. The camera still has a stand. The face still has to read.

Ink Riot vs Collage

Collage is cut pieces with dry edges. Ink riot is liquid in air. If you can peel a layer off the frame, you wanted collage. If it should look wet, you wanted this.

When should I use Ink Riot?

Titles, music, a character whose interior spills. Skip it for procedural coverage and any beat that needs a clean eyeline.

How do I prompt Ink Riot for AI image or video?

Name the person, lock the camera, name the key, then: Ink riot around [Subject], black and color blooming in liquid, calligraphy as explosion, a page that fights. Keep the eyes. One ink palette.

entries.title: Fallen Angel
entries.text:
Fallen Angel

Fallen angel, the fallen angel look, is holy light after the drop: a shaft of dirty church air, low-key flesh, wrecked wings implied by cloth, shadow, or light. The face is the altar, and costume is optional.

Create this Fallen Angel

Narrative function

The fall already happened. You are photographing the minute after: a nave, a cliff, a rooftop, a person in wrecked pale fabric with the head slightly bowed.

The camera stays still enough that the shaft of light can judge. Wings can be a coat, a shadow on stone, or nothing.

Literal feathers often cheapen the theology. It is the wrong tool for Halloween, superhero sheen, or a romance that still believes in rescue.

If the light is pretty and the wings are stock white, you shot a carnival float.

How it works

Eye height or slightly low in a nave or on a cliff. 35mm to 50mm.

Key is a high dirty window or a hard shaft camera-left, pews or rock falling to black. Low-Key Lighting contrast.

Skin like painted wood, not beauty oil. Cloth that can read as ruined wings without a feather store.

Prompt: Fallen-angel image of [Subject], wrecked wings implied, church light, a holy fall, beauty after the drop.

When to use it

Grief, blasphemy, a portrait that should feel judged: the person in the aisle, head bowed, dust in the shaft. Do not use it as a costume still with white wings and a clean key.

Compared with similar shots

Epiphany is revelation light that arrives as knowledge. Fallen angel is the same sacred air after failure.

Low-Key Lighting is the contrast without the theology. Silhouette deletes the face.

Here the face stays, half-lit, already fallen.

EpiphanyUnderstanding should be visible.

Low-Key LightingMystery, crime, or moral night.

AgamemnonMake them ancient and doomed.

In film

Wings of Desire treats angels as watchers in real air and coats. The Prophecy treats the holy as violent and tired.

Light is the theology. You are not copying a still.

Prompt it

Place the body, the shaft, and the dark. Fallen-angel image of [Subject], wrecked wings implied, church light, a holy fall, beauty after the drop.

Add nave or cliff, high dirty window camera-left, low-key, no superhero sheen, feathers optional and wrecked. Lock the camera.

Use in Image Generator

Fallen-angel image of [Subject], wrecked wings implied, church light, a holy fall, beauty after the drop.

What usually goes wrong

The usual cousin is a stock angel with white wings, or a generic Low-Key Lighting beauty. The tell is carnival feathers and a clean key.

Fix it: cut the feathers, keep the shaft, wreck the cloth, hold the face.

Questions

What is Fallen Angel in film?

A sacred low-key portrait after a fall: church or cliff light, wrecked wings implied, the face as altar. It is a lighting and costume recipe, not a camera move.

Fallen Angel vs Epiphany

Epiphany is light as knowledge arriving. Fallen angel is holy air after the drop, grace already ruined. Same shaft, different tense.

When should I use Fallen Angel?

On grief, blasphemy, or a judged portrait. Skip Halloween wings, superhero posters, and any beat that still wants rescue lighting.

How do I prompt Fallen Angel for AI image or video?

entries.title: Fairytale Castle
entries.text:
Fairytale Castle

Fairytale castle, the fairytale castle look, puts storybook stone and impossible turrets around a small figure, with dusk treated as illustration. Place first, person second: the name is a location law, not a camera move.

Create this Fairytale Castle

Narrative function

The arrival, the exile, the love story that needs a kingdom: a causeway, window grids, indigo-and-gold hour, one person small enough that the building still speaks. Stone should look drawn and real at once, like a children's plate that grew up.

Weather has to exist. A plastic CGI battlement with no hour is a matte, not this look.

It is the wrong tool for a tourist establishing shot of a real European site, unless tourists are the joke. If the figure is hero-large, the castle becomes a backdrop and the tale dies.

How it works

Wide locked camera, slightly low or eye height on the path, 24mm to 35mm. The figure occupies a third or less.

Key is dusk: indigo air, gold on stone edges. Ask for illustration-grade stone and photochemical haze, not game-engine brick.

Name the path to the door. Prompt: Fairytale-castle world around [Subject], storybook stone, impossible turrets, dusk as illustration.

When to use it

An arrival at a kingdom, an exile looking back, a love story that needs architecture as fate. Do not use it as a postcard of a real castle with a couple in the foreground.

Compared with similar shots

Magical Realism keeps real air and adds one impossible law. Fairytale castle makes the architecture itself a tale.

Diorama is toy scale on a table. Lost in a Book uses a page as the door into that world.

Magical RealismMiracle without spectacle.

DioramaShrink the epic until it fits a shelf.

AgamemnonMake them ancient and doomed.

In film

The Fall builds kingdoms as illustrated space around a body. Pan's Labyrinth lets stone and dusk obey storybook law.

Borrow the law of space, not a studio's castle.

Prompt it

Start with the building, then the small person. Fairytale-castle world around [Subject], storybook stone, impossible turrets, dusk as illustration.

Add causeway, window grids, indigo-gold hour, 24mm lock-off, figure small, photochemical air. No plastic battlements.

Use in Image Generator

What usually goes wrong

Generic fantasy mattes with no weather, or a tourist wide. The tell is game-engine brick and a hero who fills the frame.

Fix it: name the hour, the path, illustration-grade stone, and one small figure.

Questions

What is Fairytale Castle in film?

A location look: impossible turrets and storybook stone at dusk, with the person small enough that the building remains the sentence. It is production design plus hour, not a crane.

Fairytale Castle vs Magical Realism

Magical realism is ordinary air with one impossible rule. Fairytale castle is architecture that already belongs to a tale. If the street is real and a fish talks, you wanted the cousin.

When should I use Fairytale Castle?

Arrivals, exile, a love story that needs a kingdom. Skip real tourist sites and any wide where the person is larger than the gate.

How do I prompt Fairytale Castle for AI image or video?

Write the castle, the path, the dusk, a small [Subject], then: Fairytale-castle world around [Subject], storybook stone, impossible turrets, dusk as illustration. Lock a wide lens. Keep the figure small.

entries.title: Comic
entries.text:
Comic

Comic, in comic book cinematography, inks a live-action frame: hard edges, halftone in the shadows, limited spots of color, a page that still has a photographed body in it. The camera still has a lens and one sun, and it is not a screenshot of a book.

Volume

Create this Comic

Narrative function

Origin stories, punchlines, a city that should look published: the person still occupies space, but print law sits on top of the photograph. One lighting direction so the ink has a sun.

No speech balloons. Models ruin letters.

Dialogue can survive if the ink is gentle and the faces stay human. It is the wrong tool when you need documentary pores and no line, or when you actually wanted full Animation.

If there is no grain or halation of a camera, you left live action and drew a still.

How it works

Lock a 35mm or 50mm at eye height. One hard or hard-soft key so edges have a side.

Ask for inked contours, halftone in shadows, a face that is still a photograph. Limited color spots.

No balloons. Prompt: Comic-book treatment of [Subject], inked edges, halftone, panel energy, a page that moves.

For video, the print holds while the body makes one small action.

When to use it

A punchline, an origin beat, a city that should look printed. Do not use it as a cartoon filter on a whispering drama, and do not add balloons.

Compared with similar shots

Animation is drawn throughout. Comic is live action wearing print.

Typography makes letters the subject. Flash Comic adds a strobe bang on top of the same ink.

Two Color is a stricter ink budget.

AnimationThe world is constructed, not captured.

TypographyThe sentence is in the shot.

AgamemnonMake them ancient and doomed.

In film

Dick Tracy uses spot color and hard makeup as print law on photographed faces. Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse is animation you may borrow as a grade language, not as a frame to copy.

The still should look printable.

Prompt it

Keep the lens and the sun, then the print. Comic-book treatment of [Subject], inked edges, halftone, panel energy, a page that moves.

Add one key direction, photographic face, no balloons, no extra media. Motion: one action, print holding.

Use in Image Generator

Comic-book treatment of [Subject], inked edges, halftone, panel energy, a page that moves.

What usually goes wrong

Over-processing into a cartoon with no lens, or stacking this with Ink Riot and oil. The tell is no camera grain and no sun.

Fix it: one light direction, halftone in shadows, face still a photograph.

Questions

What is Comic in film?

Live-action coverage wearing print law: inked edges, halftone, limited color, a photographed body. The camera still has a lens. It is not a scan of a comic page.

Comic vs Animation

Animation is drawn as the whole image. Comic keeps photographic structure and adds ink and halftone. If there is no lens, you left this look.

When should I use Comic?

Origin beats, punchlines, a published city. Skip it when you need plain documentary skin, and skip balloons.

How do I prompt Comic for AI image or video?

Name subject, lens, and one key, then: Comic-book treatment of [Subject], inked edges, halftone, panel energy, a page that moves. Forbid speech balloons. Keep the face photographic.

entries.title: Cold Vision
entries.text:
Cold Vision

Cold vision, the cold vision look, reads the world as temperature: either an arctic photochemical grade with breath and ice, or a thermal false-color overlay with heat edges. Empathy is not in the palette, so pick one sensor and keep it.

Volume

Create this Cold Vision

Narrative function

Hunts, winter war, a stalker POV: faces become warmer than walls if you are in thermal, or paler than snow if you are in climate. The camera can be lock-off, handheld, or a device POV, but the seeing logic cannot change mid-shot.

Kindness dies in this grade unless the joke is cruelty. It is the wrong tool for a Christmas romance, a beauty key, or a teal wash that only makes skin pale.

If there is no breath, ice, or heat edge, you shot a cool LUT.

How it works

Choose one: (1) arctic still, 35mm, breath visible, ice in the air, hard winter sun or overcast white, photochemical blues, or (2) thermal/false-color overlay, readable human hotter than the room, device frame optional but no HUD letters. Do not mix Night Vision green unless that is the device.

Prompt: Cold vision of [Subject], arctic grade, thermal edges, a world seen as temperature and threat.

When to use it

A hunt through snow, a stalker watching heat, a winter war still. Do not use it as teal-and-sad on a love scene unless cruelty is the point.

Compared with similar shots

Thermal is the device overlay as such. Night Vision is green intensification, a different sensor.

Cool Blue is white-balance weather without a seeing-device or ice logic. Cold vision is the named recipe that must pick one of those physics and commit.

ThermalSee temperature, not light.

Night VisionSomeone is hunting in the dark.

Cool BlueCold institutions, night, or alienation.

In film

The Revenant is winter as climate: breath, ice, unkind daylight. The Thing is isolation in cold rooms and a world read as threat.

Name the device if you want a thermal overlay rather than weather.

Prompt it

Name the sensor, then the body. Cold vision of [Subject], arctic grade, thermal edges, a world seen as temperature and threat.

Add either breath and ice with a winter key, or false-color heat with a readable face. One logic.

No night-vision green unless you mean that tube.

Use in Image Generator

Cold vision of [Subject], arctic grade, thermal edges, a world seen as temperature and threat.

What usually goes wrong

A teal grade with pale skin, or a mash of thermal plus Night Vision. The tell is no breath, no ice, no heat edge.

Fix it: pick climate or device, show the physics, hold the face.

Questions

What is Cold Vision in film?

A seeing recipe: arctic climate with breath and ice, or thermal false-color with heat edges. It treats the world as temperature and threat, not as a sad blue LUT.

Cold Vision vs Thermal

Thermal is a specific false-color device look. Cold vision may use that overlay, or it may be photochemical winter. If you want the device, say thermal. If you want climate, show breath and ice.

When should I use Cold Vision?

Hunts, winter war, stalker POV. Skip Christmas romance and any beauty key that only wants pale skin.

How do I prompt Cold Vision for AI image or video?

Pick one sensor. Then: Cold vision of [Subject], arctic grade, thermal edges, a world seen as temperature and threat. Add breath and ice, or a heat-edge overlay, and a readable human.

entries.title: Casual Monster Slayer
entries.text:
Casual Monster Slayer

Casual monster slayer is deadpan heroism in ordinary clothes: supermarket wardrobe, impossible creature work, the same naturalistic light on both. The joke is register clash, and the camera should look like coverage of a commute, not a poster.

Volume

Create this Casual Monster Slayer

Narrative function

Keep the tote bag. Make the dragon expensive.

A person in a hoodie or an undershirt does creature work as if it were a chore, then wants to get home. Handheld or a simple lock-off.

If the camera goes baroque, the gag dies and you have a grimdark poster with a hoodie. It is the wrong tool when the hero is already designed as a warrior, or when you wanted a win pose.

Mighty fighter is that posed cousin. This one still has dirty sneakers.

How it works

Eye height, 35mm, handheld or lock-off. Describe the mundane outfit in boring detail, then put the creature or weapon in the same key: available street, kitchen practical, overcast.

Same grade on both. No rim that turns them into a sprite.

Prompt: Casual monster-slayer of [Subject], everyday clothes, impossible creature work, deadpan heroism, a commute that includes a dragon.

When to use it

Comedy-horror, a trailer still, a hero who wants to finish and go home: Shaun in the street, Jack in the alley. Do not use it for a grimdark champion poster.

Compared with similar shots

Mighty Fighter is the win pose, toy-box stance, cabinet art. Action Figure is plastic merchandise.

Casual monster slayer keeps grocery-store wardrobe and ordinary light on extraordinary work.

Shaun of the Dead puts cricket-bat labor in daylight streets. Big Trouble in Little China puts a truck driver in impossible creature work.

A register-clash recipe: everyday clothes, impossible creature work, deadpan coverage. The camera looks like a commute. The threat does not.

entries.title: Canvas
entries.text:
Canvas

Canvas, the canvas painting look, is a photographic subject wearing oil: visible bristle, canvas tooth, thicker paint in the lights, eyes that still look. It is not a slider named oil: brushwork has direction and weight.

Create this Canvas

Narrative function

Portraits that should feel made by hand, credits, a memory: you still compose a shot of a person, then the stock becomes paint. The camera is usually a portrait distance, locked, so stroke direction can be read.

If you cannot see a stroke, it is a grade, not canvas. It is the wrong tool when you wanted unfinished line, optical dabs, or wet process.

Those are sketch, Monet muse, and hand-paint. A luxury ad may want magazine instead.
